headline.title: We searched "chiropractor Anniesland Glasgow". Your own website appeared in none of the 14 results.
headline.detail: Your booking page came first, then directory pages (NPN, Poyst, WhatClinic, Fresha, Yabsta) describing chiropractors in their own words. Someone comparing clinics never reaches a page that explains your approach.

summary: Glasgow Spinal Care has something rare: 83 reviews at 4.8 from patients who say you explain every step and never over-promise, plus on-site spinal X-ray. But in our search, your own website didn't appear at all, and a chiropractor a mile away with 54 five-star reviews looks just as good on a listing.

search.result: Your Jane booking page came first, followed by NPN, Poyst, WhatClinic, Fresha and other directories. Your own website (chiropractor-glasgow.uk) did not appear in the 14 results.
search.meaning: People searching for exactly what you do find a booking form or a directory, not the story of why patients trust you.

visibility: In our search for a chiropractor in Anniesland, your booking page appeared but your own website did not. Clinics with more reviews and longer hours appear right alongside you in Glasgow listings.
lead: Patients praise Dr Morris for explaining every step: no surprises, no over-promising.
On-site spinal X-ray, with referrals accepted from other clinics.
A welcoming reception team, named in reviews, which reassures nervous first-timers.
lose: Nobody can book with you on a Saturday; several clinics nearby open on Saturdays and one is open seven days.
A clinic in the city centre has 429 reviews, so at a glance it looks like the safer choice.
Your strengths (X-ray, honesty, Gonstead technique) only live in reviews, not on a page that new patients read.

gaps.title: Weekend back pain goes elsewhere
gaps.detail: Backs give out on Saturdays too. When you're closed and there's no page explaining when the next slot is, people book whichever clinic is open.

gaps.title: Your honesty is invisible
gaps.detail: 'No over-promising' is a powerful reason to choose you, but someone comparing listings never reads it.

gaps.title: Happy patients aren't asked for reviews
gaps.detail: 83 reviews is strong, but a city-centre clinic has 429. Without an automatic review request after each visit, that gap keeps growing.

actions.title: Give patients one page that explains your approach
actions.why: X-ray, Gonstead, clear explanations and real reviews in one place turns comparison shoppers into bookings.

actions.title: Ask every happy patient for a review automatically
actions.why: A short message after each visit steadily closes the review gap with larger clinics.

actions.title: Pin your X-ray and referral service on your Google profile
actions.why: Doable today: other chiropractors and patients searching for spinal imaging will find you first.

plan.title: Your new website with booking built in
plan.detail: Your approach, team and X-ray service, with one-tap booking from any phone.

plan.title: Automatic review requests
plan.detail: A friendly message after each appointment, so happy patients become five-star reviews.

plan.title: Reminders and recall
plan.detail: Maintenance-visit reminders that go out by themselves, so patients stay on track.

plan.title: Your first monthly report
plan.detail: Where you stand against Glasgow West End clinics, and what to do next.

scenario: It's Saturday morning in Jordanhill and a dad's back locks as he lifts his son into the car. He searches "chiropractor near me" and sees your listing, closed until Monday, next to a booking-site page for a clinic open today. He books there, and by Monday he has a new chiropractor. (Illustration.)
nochange: Your reviews keep growing slowly, but every weekend and every evening, people who would love your honest approach meet a listing or a directory instead. The clinics with more reviews and longer hours keep looking like the default choice.
